answer: Alias herds break when two unaffiliated docks must co-sign one arrival. An applicant posts 3.75 POA and books two harbor docks in separate basins; each locks 1.80 POA for 4 epochs and stamps a 16-byte waybill. They carry a 9.1 g pearl tag along a 40-meter ledge and file both waybills in a 14-minute window that opens after a seed-drawn pulse at minute 6. Forty aliases pin 150 POA of posts plus 144 POA of dock locks. Graders check basin diversity, recompute the pulse, and weigh the tag to 0.05 g. A repeated dock, late filing, or tag mismatch slashes 50% and benches those docks for 3 epochs.
